def match(pattern: str, text: str) -> bool:
    """
    Implements a recursive approach for basic regex matching. 
    The function supports matching of literal characters, 
    '.' (any character), '*' (zero or more of the preceding element), 
    and '+' (one or more of the preceding element) using recursion 
    with memoization for improved efficiency.
    """
    
    memo = {}
    
    def is_match(p: str, t: str) -> bool:
        if (p, t) in memo:
            return memo[(p, t)]
        
        if not p:
            result = not t
            memo[(p, t)] = result
            return result

        first_match = bool(t) and (p[0] == t[0] or p[0] == '.')

        if len(p) >= 2 and p[1] in ['*', '+']:
            if p[1] == '*':
                result = (is_match(p[2:], t) or 
                          (first_match and is_match(p, t[1:])))
                memo[(p, t)] = result
                return result
            elif p[1] == '+' and first_match:
                result = is_match(p, t[1:]) or is_match(p[2:], t)
                memo[(p, t)] = result
                return result

        result = first_match and is_match(p[1:], t[1:])
        memo[(p, t)] = result
        return result

    return is_match(pattern, text)
